images.filename: Lichfield Cathedral Organ, Staffordshire, UK - Diliff.jpg
images.caption: George Holdich (14 August 1816 – 30 July 1896) was a British organist and organ builder based in London. In 1851, he produced a pipe organ that was exhibited at the Great Exhibition. This photograph shows Holdich's best-known achievement, the new organ for Lichfield Cathedral, installed in 1861. The instrument, which has 52 stops, was the first in England to have a full pedal specification of stops as was customary among organs in continental Europe.

images.caption: Lichfield Cathedral (St. Mary & St. Chad), 4 July 2016. The original cathedral was founded in 700 in the then Kingdom of Mercia. The present one was built in 1195-1330. It is the only English Cathedral with three spires - 'The Ladies of the Vale'. The cathedral was very heavily damaged in three sieges in the English Civil War and not finally restored until the 19th Century. Pictured is the Decorated Quire (1200) and South Aisle (1260).
